research_question: Among community-dwelling adults aged 60 years or older, what is the immediate post-intervention effect of CBT or behaviour-change interventions delivered alone or with exercise (including multicomponent programmes, motivational support, Tai Chi plus CBT, and exercise plus motivational interviewing), compared with usual care, no intervention, or attention/discussion/education control, on fear of falling or falls-related self-efficacy in randomized trials?
treatment_label: CBT or behaviour-change intervention, alone or combined with exercise/Tai Chi
control_label: Usual care, no intervention, or attention/discussion/education control
outcome_description: Fear of falling/falls-related self-efficacy at the first assessment after the intervention ended, preferably within approximately one month; if only later follow-up is available, use the earliest reported assessment. Extract post-intervention mean, SD, and analyzed participant count per arm, preferring post-intervention scores over change scores. Select one measure per study in this order: FES-I or short FES-I; modified FES, FES, Swedish FES-S, or ABC; then a single-item fear question. Orient all scales so lower values indicate less fear: retain FES-I and similar concern scales as reported and multiply confidence scales such as FES-S, mFES, and ABC by −1 before computing the effect. Do not pool later follow-ups when an earlier post-intervention assessment exists, or outcomes of activity avoidance, depression, anxiety, quality of life, falls counts, or adverse events. Deduplicate multiple trial reports and use the short-term or primary report. Include every eligible CBT/behaviour-change arm; where eligible arms share a control, split the control sample size equally. Prefer cluster-adjusted results; otherwise reduce effective sample sizes using an appropriate design-effect adjustment and report the assumptions.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges' g denotes less fear of falling or greater falls-related confidence in the intervention group and therefore favors the CBT/behaviour-change intervention; for reporting under the user's requested treatment-minus-control convention, reverse this sign so that SMD below 0 favors intervention.
search_queries: cognitive behavioural therapy fear of falling older adults randomized trial
behaviour change falls self efficacy community dwelling older people controlled trial
A Matter of Balance Tai Chi CBT fear of falling randomized
inclusion_criteria: Randomized or cluster-randomized trials enrolling community-dwelling people aged 60 years or older.

Interventions containing a CBT or explicit behaviour-change/motivational component, delivered alone or with exercise or Tai Chi, compared with usual care, no intervention, or an attention/discussion/education control.
Quantitative fear-of-falling or falls-related self-efficacy data reported at the first available post-intervention assessment.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original eligible randomized empirical study; systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, theoretical papers, and nonrandomized studies are excluded.

No comparison between an eligible CBT/behaviour-change treatment and a control condition; this includes exercise-only, education-only, home-modification, or hip-protector interventions with no CBT/behaviour-change component.
No quantitative outcome data capable of producing an effect size, such as means and SDs, t/F statistics, proportions, or odds ratios, after reasonable attempts to derive or obtain the required data.
Completely unrelated to the research topic, including studies outside community-dwelling adults aged 60 years or older or studies not assessing fear of falling/falls-related self-efficacy.
moderators_to_extract: intervention composition (CBT alone, CBT plus exercise, Tai Chi plus CBT, motivational/behaviour-change exercise programme)
control type (usual care/no intervention versus attention/discussion/education)
delivery format and setting (individual, group, home, community, remote)
mean participant age and proportion female
trial design and analysis (individual versus cluster randomization; clustering adjustment method)
effect_size_note: Pool standardized mean differences as Hedges' g with a random-effects model using post-intervention scores. The user's requested presentation is treatment minus control after orienting all measures so lower scores mean less fear; therefore SMD < 0 favors intervention. Use one prioritized fear-of-falling measure and one first post-intervention timepoint per study. For shared controls, divide the control sample size equally across eligible comparisons without changing its mean or SD. For unadjusted cluster trials, apply a design effect based on cluster size and ICC, using an externally justified ICC only if necessary and documenting sensitivity analyses. Report heterogeneity (tau², I², and Q), confidence and prediction intervals where feasible, influence/outlier analyses, risk-of-bias assessment, certainty of evidence, and PRISMA 2020 study flow.
